text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGED oncall kai for SEGV crashloop on runtime pods in gpu-pool-03 (gpulab-03, gpulab-04). 500s observed, approx 12% of hosted requests failing. Auto-mitigation attempted: restarted pods, but crashloop continues. Paging window started now.

kai: I'm oncall, looking. Can someone drop recent pod logs and dmesg?

shaun: pushing logs now. kubectl -n redwood get pods -l app=runtime -o wide | grep gpulab-03
shaun: runtime-pod-rt-7f8bd  CrashLoopBackOff  gpulab-03  2/3 restarts

eli: copy of last stderr from runtime container: 
```
[2026-03-15T01:12:05Z] runtime: segfault at 0 ip 0x7f8b12e6 sp 0x7ffd1e4c error 4 in trt_llm.so[7f8b120000+3a000]
Stack trace (most recent call first):
  0x7f8b12e6  trt_infer::execute_kernels+0x46
  0x7f8b9f3  vllm::Executor::run+0x253
  0x4008f2  main+0x1a2
  libc.so.6(__libc_start_main)+0xf0
```

kai: looks like a fused/quant kernel in TRT (trt_llm). Could be NVLINK/driver weirdness or bad JITed kernel. Is there a pattern across hosts?

miriam: gpulab-04 shows same segfaults at nearly same time. Noticed node had an nvlink reset in kernel ring: see dmesg snippet: 
```
[  123.456789] NVRM: GPU at 0000:3b:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[  123.456800] nvrm: NvRmNotifyPowerManager... resetting
[  123.456812] nvlink: link error recovery triggered
```

kai: NVLINK link errors + trt fused kernel segfault = possible driver/hw flake. Initial plan: 1) cordon gpulab-03/04 and drain runtime pods off these nodes to reduce customer impact; 2) enable fallback runtime variant that disables fused kernels/optimizations; 3) open a short incident channel to SRE to check for hardware faults and driver reboots.

eli: prepared a rollout: set ENV REDWOOD_RT_DISABLE_FUSED=1 in runtime Deployment and bump to canary 10%. Command: 
```
kubectl -n redwood set env deployment/runtime REDWOOD_RT_DISABLE_FUSED=1
kubectl -n redwood rollout restart deployment/runtime --record
```

shaun: can we avoid full rollout; do a node-level evict first? draining will cause restarts which may hit same crash on other nodes. The env var + canary is safer.

kai: agree. Start canary now and watch.

infra-bot: canary started (deployment/runtime -> new replicaset rts-canary-02). 1 pod scheduled on gpulab-07.

miriam: routing policy: switch 30% of traffic to cached responses and fallback model on hosted API (to reduce failed requests). Doing a temporary routing rule in the LB. @cs-lead FYI, will reduce latency for some customers but avoids 500s.

cs-lead: noted, will post a message to affected customers and pause automated job retries. Drafting update.

kai: canary pod logs show no segfaults after 8m. Good sign. Meanwhile, gpulab-03 still flapping. I'm going to cordon gpulab-03 and run a soft drain to move remaining runtime pods.

shaun: running: `kubectl cordon gpulab-03 && kubectl drain gpulab-03 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --timeout=5m`

infra-bot: node gpulab-03 cordoned. pods evicted: runtime-pod-rt-7f8bd -> scheduled to gpulab-08.

eli: after evict, runtime-pod on gpulab-08 started and handled traffic successfully for 6m, then OOM on kv-cache and restarted (not segfault). Increasing `REDWOOD_CACHE_MAX_BYTES` for that pod's env to 12GB as temporary mitigation.

kai: the pattern is: node-level NVLINK reset -> some lingering kernel state -> segfault in TRT fused path on next inference call. Looks hardware/driver-adjacent. We'll mark these nodes for hardware triage and replace if needed.

miriam: triage steps for SRE/hardware team: collect nvrm logs, run `nvidia-smi -q`, capture ECC/counter stats, escalate to cloud provider if persistent. I'm opening an ops ticket.

shaun: we've slipped error budget for two customers. cs-lead, can you send the customer note with status + ETA for remediation? Mention routing fallback and canary rollout.

cs-lead: sending now. Message: "We detected a runtime crashloop affecting ~12% of requests in us-west. Traffic has been routed to a fallback model to prevent 500s. We're rolling out a safe runtime variant and evacuating impacted nodes. ETA for full restoration: 60-90 minutes. We will follow up with root cause once SRE completes diagnostics." Will paste thread link into ticket.

kai: update after 34m: canary at 20% shows stable pods with REDWOOD_RT_DISABLE_FUSED=1. Crashloops stopped for canary pods. Rolling to 50% then 100% if stable for next 20m.

eli: noted a single pod on gpulab-09 hit an OOM during this; increased eviction grace and raised cache limit as mentioned. No new segfaults.

infra-bot: rollout at 50% complete. No new segfaults observed in last 12m.

miriam: doing oncall handoff in 30m to @eli for follow-up (driver logs, vendor escalation). If anything spikes, call me.

kai: starting postmortem notes: timeline, mitigation (canary env var), nodes cordoned, fallback routing, customer comms. Will include stack traces and nvlink dmesg.

shaun: question for infra: should we add a temporary proactive scheduler rule to avoid gpulab-03/04 until hardware is validated?

infra-bot: yes, nodes gpulab-03,gpulab-04 are set to unschedulable for runtime pods (taint: runtime-problem=true:NoSchedule).

eli: vendor update: opened ticket with GPU vendor, attached kernel dmesg and logs. They requested full `nvidia-bug-report.sh` output and suggested driver rollback as last resort.

miriam: final update before handoff: canary -> 100% complete, no segfaults for 45m, customer impact reduced to <0.5% errors. Keeping nodes cordoned and hardware ticket open. Oncall handoff to eli at 3667811600.

kai: thanks everyone. I'll convert this thread into the incident postmortem and tag owners for follow-up actions: hardware replacement, kernel/driver monitoring, and an automated canary for fused-kernel failures. :thumbsup:

eli: taking over oncall. I'll follow up on vendor, hardware replacement plan, and schedule regen tests once nodes replaced.

incident-bot: Incident closed for paging window. Follow-up timeline: postmortem draft due in 24h, customer follow-up in 48h.
